taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station Bank-road (Bori Metropolis). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 640 | 5.21 | 5.21
2 | 934 | 8.58 | 13.8
3 | 2594 | 84.1 | 97.9
4 | 4386 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as AK-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: Bank-road (Bori Metropolis)
Curve type: A (note: resistivities rise consistently 640 → 934 → 2594 → 4386 ohm-m, giving AA by the layer-triad rule, which reduces to a single A-type; this corrects the "AK-type" label on file)
Aquifer depth: 13.8 m – 97.9 m (resistive Layer 3, 2594 ohm-m, likely sand/gravel aquifer; the underlying Layer 4, >97.9 m, may also be aquiferous)
Recommendation: Plan the borehole to penetrate through the 13.8–97.9 m resistive zone, with casing set through the upper conductive layers (0–13.8 m) to prevent collapse; confirm aquifer continuation beyond 97.9 m by advancing a few additional metres with cuttings/geophysical logging before finalizing total depth.
